statement: For every infinite λ, there is an acyclic map BS_λ→∨_λ S² with S_λ nonabelian simple of size λ and BS_λ two-dimensional; it satisfies R2 for all μ<λ. Therefore dimension alone bounds no μ, even for nonaspherical targets.

A split cellular-chain retraction gives the actual acyclic map to the wedge of λ two-spheres. This does not settle infinite μ for a fixed target such as S².

statement: For every q≥1 a finite aspherical surface block M_q has geometric dimension at most 2, contains π₁Σ_q injectively, and kills its fundamental H₂ class; gluing it along any map Σ_q→an aspherical X preserves asphericity and π₁-injectivity in dimension at most max(dim X,3).

notes: Positive genus is explicit. The construction uses C(L), deletion of one cone corner, dual-tree collapses, an oriented cubical 3-cycle, the CAT(0) radial retraction, and the branched-cover link argument. The proof extends Lemma 6.2 from 2D X to arbitrary aspherical X.

statement: For every infinite λ there is a nonabelian simple acyclic group A_λ of cardinality λ with a classifying CW model of dimension at most 3 and at most λ cells. All homomorphisms to groups of cardinality less than λ are trivial.
manuscript_pages_settled: A3(iii): arbitrary-cardinal finite-dimensional acyclic simple groups
notes: Actual 3D CW inclusions alternate HNN commutator embeddings and surface-block attachments. The map from the direct sum of surface H₂ groups is injective, so H₃ never grows. New H₂ remains free; countable unions kill H₁ and H₂. Alternate with the simple envelope. No finite-dimensional inference is made from torsion groups or mitotic envelopes.

statement: For connected finite-dimensional W, every cardinal μ, and every infinite λ>μ bounding its cells, R2 admits |P|=|G|=λ, P nonabelian simple, and a BG with at most λ cells of dimension at most max(dim W,3). Thus the requested dimension is available for all dim W≥3 and all μ; dimensions ≤1 are settled by identities.
manuscript_pages_settled: A3(iii): all target dimensions except the remaining infinite-μ two-dimensional case
notes: Equivariant proof over Z[π₁W] retains the initial H₂(W̃) summand, including torsion. Relative simple stages produce projective H₂ kernel; λ zero-boundary HNN marker cells split off a free summand and make the kernel free by stabilization. Surface-block stages attach all deck translates, keep higher homology, give induced H₁ of projective dimension ≤1, and retain a free H₂ kernel. At the union the π-cover comparison is a homology isomorphism; its bounded-below free mapping cone is contractible over the group ring, proving all local coefficients.
